summary: Ledge-side light at the eastern end of Lake Ontario, Henderson NY: shown from 1838, rebuilt in 1869, automated after 1946, now a private home.

lens.note: Revolving fifth-order Fresnel lens fitted 1857 (LighthouseFriends); archive: original optic fifth-order Fresnel.

light.note: Focal plane 58 ft (17.7 m) after the 1901 raise (archive Light List 1901; LighthouseFriends); 1926 characteristic alternating red and white; 1947 red flash every 10 s.

structures.note: Old tower, converted to a private home; archive: square, brick; LighthouseFriends and the Society news: stone. Raised 20 ft in 1901.
White skeleton tower near the shore; light at 25 ft focal plane (LighthouseFriends); 'steel skeleton tower' (Society news).
Archive: 3 storage buildings and foundations of an 1830 tower.

staffing.note: Last keeper left November 1946; light automated shortly after (LighthouseFriends; Society news).

access.note: Privately owned. LighthouseFriends: grounds, dwelling and tower closed. Archive: not open to the public.

visit.note: Private home. Do not land or walk onto the private grounds.

events.note: Light established after Congress's 1837 appropriation; Platt's inspection report dated November 26, 1838 (as quoted by LighthouseFriends).
New tower; sources disagree on brick or stone.
Concrete foundation for an oil house; metal work for the oil house purchased (Board, fiscal year ended 30 June 1896).
Oil house metal erected; old oil room fitted as a living room (Board, fiscal year ended 30 June 1897).
Tower built up 20 ft: focal plane 38 ft to 58 ft; painted white; flash interval 2 min to 1 min.
Mial Eugene Eggleston transferred to the station on February 15, 1906, replacing Alden C. Stevens.
Steam barge Iona burned on Lake Ontario on May 18, 1912; crew reached shore. Sources disagree on distances, cargo, crew count and landing place.
Archive record: year discontinued 1945. Other sources differ (see notes).
Discontinued for the season in November 1946, when the last keeper left (LighthouseFriends).
Characteristic changed to a red flash every ten seconds as part of automation.
White skeleton tower built near the shore; light at 25 ft focal plane; old tower's light discontinued.
Sold off for $9,107 to a private owner.
Fire in a nearby barn spread out of control and nearly destroyed the lighthouse.
Private buyers bought the station in 2002; the structure was found unsound and gutted before restoration.

keepers.name: Mial Eugene Eggleston

wrecks.outcome: Steam barge burned on Lake Ontario: about 15 miles off Oswego (NOAA) or 25 miles offshore (LighthouseFriends). NOAA: captain and 12 crew took to one boat and landed at Henderson Harbor; LighthouseFriends: ten survivors, cared for at the station (landing place differs). Counts and cargo differ between the two sources.

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends: Congress appropriated funds on March 3, 1837, and the light was finished and operational by the end of 1838 (Platt's report dated November 26, 1838). The Society's news item and the archive's place record give 1838. The 1830 date is not explained by any source read; the archive lists foundations of an 1830 tower on the site.

The archive's place record gives 53.25 ft (16.2 m) from base of structure to the centre of the lantern. The record's 22.0 m does not match that figure; check the source of the 22.0 m before changing it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1838 is the first lighting: the 1837 appropriation built the light, the November 1838 report describes it, and the Society's news item and place record agree. The 1869 date is the present tower. The 1830 foundations are unexplained (see notes).

Not resolved: NOAA and LighthouseFriends differ on distance offshore (15 vs 25 miles), cargo (1,000 vs 450 tons), crew count (captain and 12 crew vs ten survivors) and landing place (Henderson Harbor vs the station). Both are stated in the story.

notes_for_editor: 1) First lighting: the archive's place record and Rowlett's directory (as the record quotes it) give 1830; the archive's place record also lists foundations of an 1830 tower. LighthouseFriends and the Society news give 1838 after an 1837 appropriation. Story states 1838 and leaves 1830 unexplained. Proposed correction to light.first_lit. 2) Tower material: archive says brick (FY place record: 'Tower Construction Material: BRICK'); LighthouseFriends and the Society news say stone. Stated as disputed in the story; not a record error. 3) Light out: archive 1945; LighthouseFriends 'discontinued for the season' November 1946 when Koepka left; 1959 when the old tower's light was replaced (LighthouseFriends and Society news). Stated as disputed. 4) Iona 1912: NOAA and LighthouseFriends disagree on distance offshore (15 vs 25 miles), cargo (1,000 vs 450 tons), crew count (captain and 12 crew, 13 people, vs ten survivors) and landing place (Henderson Harbor vs the station). LighthouseFriends cites the Watertown Daily Times, 20 May 1912; that newspaper was not read. Chronicling America searches for the Iona rescue (New York papers, 1912) returned no relevant page. 5) Corpus grep for Stony Point (New York) found Life-Saving Service station and wreck tables for Lake Ontario (not used: counts read by column position) and Board entries for FY1896, FY1897 and FY1900 (cited, all three page numbers checked against the running heads: FY1896 p.129 index entry; FY1897 p.145 between the 145 and 146 running heads; FY1900 p.154 between the 154 and 155 heads). Hudson River 'Stony Point' entries in the Board reports are a different station and were excluded. 6) Roster matched by the archive's own place record (the 'Principal Lighthouse Keeper' heading). LighthouseFriends' head-keeper list also includes Eliza Stevens (1906), with no detail; the story says so (earlier draft wrongly said LighthouseFriends did not mention her). Relationship to Alden C. Stevens unknown. 7) Keepers' names of private owners of the 1960s-2000s are omitted. The 2002 buyers are named in the Society news URL (a public podcast) and in LighthouseFriends; the story does not name them. 8) Owners' restoration and current status not independently verified. 9) The Society news page and LighthouseFriends both paraphrase a 1959 change; they agree on the skeleton tower. 10) Eggleston's Charlotte (Rochester) service rests only on LighthouseFriends; recorded as other_stations with no id because the station's map id was not checked. 11) The Board's FY1897 entry is on printed page 145 (between the running heads 145 and 146 in the OCR); the scan is n407. 12) Koepka is spelled 'Wylie E.' by the archive and 'Wiley Koepka' by LighthouseFriends; the story uses the archive form. 13) Wrong-fact check: the record's 'structures.tower.height_m 22.0' does not match the archive's 53.25 ft (16.2 m) to the lantern centre; check the source of the 22.0 before changing it.
